samples.question: This image is a record of a pouring experiment, drawn as two stacked panels separated by a horizontal rule. Above the rule stand four open vessels. The vessels are deliberately built to different widths, and each one holds a solid slab of liquid resting on its floor: one red slab, one blue slab, one green slab and one orange slab. Below the rule stand four narrow measuring tubes. Every tube was manufactured to one and the same width, and every tube is shaded in one identical gray, so nothing about a tube's shading identifies where its contents came from. Each vessel above was emptied into exactly one tube below and each tube received exactly one vessel. No tube stands underneath the vessel it received, so vertical position is uninformative. Pouring deforms a slab of liquid but destroys none of it, so the shaded area inside a tube is equal to the shaded area of the slab that was poured into it. Since the vessels were built to different widths, a tall narrow slab can carry less liquid than a short wide one, and the tallest slab above need not correspond to the tallest column below. A black triangle is printed above exactly one of the tubes. Which colour was the liquid that was poured into the marked tube? Answer with red, blue, green, or orange.
